phase1.intro:
You've technically met a few of these already, buried inside other lessons' broken code — this lesson just puts names to faces.

Which theme do you want to look at first?

dialogue: [[key:Missing or invalid data]]: [[term:NullPointerException]] happens the instant you call a method on a null reference — `String str = null; str.length();` has nothing to call length() on.
[[term:NumberFormatException]] is its cousin for parsing — `Integer.parseInt("123abc")` fails because that text simply isn't a valid number.

stickyNote.flavor: ❓ calling on null, or parsing garbage as a number
stickyNote.definition: NullPointerException fires calling a method on null. NumberFormatException fires parsing text that isn't a valid number.

topics.buttonText: What's the difference between ArrayIndexOutOfBounds and IndexOutOfBounds?
dialogue: [[key:Going out of bounds]]: [[term:ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException]] for arrays, [[term:IndexOutOfBoundsException]] for Lists like ArrayList — both mean you asked for a position that doesn't actually exist, index 5 in a 3-element array or `list.get(5)` on a 3-element list.

stickyNote.flavor: 📏 asking for a position that doesn't exist
stickyNote.definition: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (arrays) and IndexOutOfBoundsException (Lists) both fire when accessing an index beyond the collection's actual size.

topics.buttonText: What about ClassCastException, ArithmeticException, and IOException?
dialogue: [[key:Type and logic mistakes]]: [[term:ClassCastException]] fires when a downcast guesses wrong, [[term:ArithmeticException]] covers math errors like dividing by zero, [[term:IllegalArgumentException]] is the one YOU throw for a caller passing an unworkable value.

On the checked side: [[term:IOException]] and [[term:FileNotFoundException]] cover things going wrong reading/writing files. [[warn:It's worth internalizing the pattern rather than memorizing this list]]: [[key:unchecked exceptions almost always mean a bug in your own code]].

stickyNote.definition: ClassCastException (bad downcast), ArithmeticException (math errors), IllegalArgumentException (bad caller input) are unchecked. IOException/FileNotFoundException are checked I/O problems.

phase1.openingDialogue: The common built-in exceptions cluster into three themes — missing data, out of bounds, and type/logic mistakes — plus checked I/O exceptions. 🗂️

phase2.explanation:
No broken code this time — just two misconceptions worth correcting before they cause real confusion later.

First: [[warn:"NullPointerException means the variable is undefined" is wrong]]. The variable exists — it's just pointing at nothing. String str = null; is a completely valid, well-defined variable; it simply holds no object to call methods on, which is exactly why str.length() has nothing to work with.

Second: [[key:IOException isn't something to shrug off]]. Files go missing, disks fill up, permissions get denied — these happen constantly in real programs, far more often than most beginners expect, and every one of them deserves a genuine recovery plan (a retry, a fallback, a clear message to the user) rather than a catch block that just prints a stack trace and moves on.

phase3.openingDialogue: Quick quiz! Which exception is this? 🤔

mcq.question:
Which exception would be thrown by the following code?

String[] names = {"Alice", "Bob"};
System.out.println(names[2]);

A) NullPointerException
B) ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
C) NumberFormatException
D) ClassCastException
E) ArithmeticException

Select the correct exception.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: NullPointerException is so notoriously common that its inventor, Tony Hoare (who introduced the null reference concept back in 1965), has publicly called it his "billion-dollar mistake" — his own estimate of the cumulative cost of bugs it's caused across the software industry since.
phase5.openingDialogue: One more thought before you go~
